page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.8xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 3.1 GHz. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs with a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration, supported by a KVM hypervisor. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and it features a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

In benchmark testing, the instance demonstrates solid mid-range performance across various compute and memory workloads. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a single-core stress-ng score of 1436.68 and a multi-core score of 30666.35, alongside a Geekbench multi-core score of 11107.0. Memory bandwidth tests show 1705.41 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 109.89 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. For specialized workloads, the server processes Redis SET operations at 28.91 million operations per second and handles static web serving throughput at 21.45 GB/sec. LLM inference speeds reach 1539.55 tokens per second for prompt processing on a small 135M model, dropping to 45.98 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

From a resource density perspective, the dedicated core allocation offers predictable CPU performance without hyperthreading overhead, which is highly efficient for workloads sensitive to CPU jitter. However, the lack of bundled local storage means all storage requirements must be met via network-attached options, which may introduce latency and additional configuration complexity. The absence of a GPU also limits its utility for large-scale deep learning tasks, though it remains a cost-effective option for standard CPU-bound applications.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated compute resources, the ecs.hfg6.8xlarge is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, multi-threaded software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and moderate-scale text or image processing tasks.
